skill.name: remotion-render
skill.description: Render React and Remotion TSX components into MP4 videos through the inference.sh CLI.
skill.summary: Render Remotion component code into configurable MP4 videos using inference.sh.
skill.author: qu-skills

security_audit.summary: The skill has legitimate Remotion rendering functionality, but it depends on the inference.sh CLI and sends TSX input to an external renderer. Most static backtick findings are Markdown formatting false positives, while the real risks are the documented belt and npx commands, broad belt tool permission, and external data transfer.

remediation.issue: Broad belt wildcard in allowed tools
remediation.suggestion: Limit allowed tools to the exact belt commands needed for login and infsh/remotion-render, or require confirmation before any other belt subcommand.

remediation.issue: Remote submission of component code and props
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before rendering that code, props, and media references are sent to inference.sh, and advise them to remove secrets and private data.

remediation.issue: External skill installation commands in documentation
remediation.suggestion: Mark npx skills add commands as optional manual setup steps and pin trusted versions or sources where possible.

static_findings.snippet: > **Install the belt CLI skill:** `npx skills add belt-sh/cli`
| `code` | string | Yes | React component TSX code. Must export default a component. |
| `composition_id` | string | No | Composition ID to render |
| `props` | object | No | Props passed to the component |
| `width` | number | No | Video width in pixels |
| `height` | number | No | Video height in pixels |
| `duration_seconds` | number | No | Video duration in seconds |
Your TSX code can import from `remotion` and `react`:
"code": "import { useCurrentFrame, useVideoConfig, spring, AbsoluteFill } from \"remotion\"; export
Render videos from React/Remotion component code via [inference.sh](https://inference.sh) CLI.
- [Running Apps](https://inference.sh/docs/apps/running) - How to run apps via CLI

semantic_findings.title: Broad CLI Permission for belt
semantic_findings.description: The front matter allows Bash(belt *), which permits any belt subcommand rather than only the render app workflow. This broad wildcard increases the impact if later instructions or user prompts steer the agent toward unintended belt actions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed-tools declaration is explicit and uses a wildcard. The risk depends on belt capabilities, so the severity is medium rather than high.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Rendering of Arbitrary TSX Input
semantic_findings.description: The skill requires React component code as input and sends it through the inference.sh renderer. Users may unintentionally upload proprietary code, embedded secrets, or sensitive props to an external service.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly describes rendering through inference.sh and shows belt app run with a code payload. This directly supports the data egress and remote execution concern.

content.value_statement: Creating MP4 videos from React animations can require local setup and render infrastructure. This skill routes Remotion TSX through inference.sh and returns a rendered video.
actual_capabilities: Render React and Remotion TSX components into MP4 videos.
Pass props into the rendered component for data-driven videos.
Configure width, height, frame rate, duration, and output codec.
Use Remotion APIs including useCurrentFrame, interpolate, spring, Sequence, and AbsoluteFill.
Run renders through the inference.sh belt CLI and receive a video output URL.
Show Python SDK patterns for batch rendering and streaming progress.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and an authenticated account.
Sends component code and props to an external rendering service.
Does not provide local validation or sandboxing for submitted TSX code.
Render success depends on supported Remotion APIs and inference.sh availability.

use_cases.title: Create Motion Graphics
use_cases.description: Render short branded animations, text reveals, and visual transitions from Remotion component descriptions.

use_cases.title: Automate Data Videos
use_cases.description: Generate videos that use props for titles, metrics, labels, or campaign-specific values.

use_cases.title: Prototype React Animation Output
use_cases.description: Convert a React animation idea into an MP4 without preparing a local Remotion render environment.

prompt_templates.title: Render a Simple Intro
prompt_templates.prompt: Render a three second Remotion video with a dark background and centered title text. Use 1920 by 1080 resolution and 30 fps.

prompt_templates.title: Render with Brand Props
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Remotion render that accepts title, subtitle, and brand color props. Use the props to produce a polished announcement video.

prompt_templates.title: Render a Sequence Animation
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Remotion component with three timed scenes using Sequence, fade transitions, and clear typography. Render it as a four second MP4.

prompt_templates.title: Render a Data-Driven Batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a reusable Remotion render plan for multiple campaign variants. Define the props, render settings, and progress tracking approach.

output_examples.input: Render a two second welcome animation with a fade-in title and 1080p output.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a rendered MP4 video URL with the requested title animation, frame rate, duration, and resolution.

output_examples.input: Create a square progress counter video that reaches 100 percent over five seconds.
output_examples.output: The output is a square MP4 with animated percentage text and timing based on the configured frame count.

output_examples.input: Render a video template with title and subtitle props for a product announcement.
output_examples.output: The result is a rendered video using the supplied prop values and the requested visual layout.

best_practices: Keep submitted TSX focused on rendering and remove secrets, tokens, and private data.
Specify duration, frame rate, width, and height before rendering to avoid unexpected output.
Use props for reusable text and data so the component can support multiple variants.
anti_patterns: Do not submit proprietary source code that is unrelated to the video render.
Do not rely on external media URLs unless they are stable and safe to share.
Do not install related skills or tools without reviewing their source and permissions.

faq.question: What does this skill render?
faq.answer: It renders React and Remotion TSX component code into MP4 video output through inference.sh.

faq.question: Does it require local Remotion setup?
faq.answer: No local Remotion project is required, but the inference.sh belt CLI and login are required.

faq.question: Can I pass custom data into a video?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill supports props that can drive titles, subtitles, metrics, colors, and other component values.

faq.question: Can it render animations using Remotion helpers?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use helpers such as useCurrentFrame, interpolate, spring, AbsoluteFill, and Sequence.

faq.question: Where is my code processed?
faq.answer: The render request is sent to inference.sh, so code and props should be treated as shared with that service.

faq.question: What should I check before rendering?
faq.answer: Confirm the render settings, remove sensitive data, and verify that any external assets are safe to access.
